newsitem.title: FRANCE: Spending by French car owners fell in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Spending by French car owners fell in 1996.

text.p: French car owners spent an average 40,559 francs ($7,020) on cars and related expenses last year, down 1.2 percent from 1995 levels, after car prices and interest rates fell, the national auto club ACN said on Tuesday.

The reduction reflected an eight percent drop in car prices as carmakers waged a price war in the French market and a six percent drop in credit costs, the ACN said. It said petrol, insurance, repair and maintenance costs rose last year.
The French spent less than German car owners, whose spending averaged 42,635 francs last year, but more than the British, who spent 37,479 francs.

Taxes represent 31 percent of total spending by French car owners, compared with 27 percent in Britain and Germany. The value added tax rate is 20.6 percent in France, 17.5 percent in Britain and 15 percent in Germany.

In the past 10 years, spending by car owners in France has climbed by a third -- it was 30,351 francs in 1987 -- exceeding inflation of 24.6 percent for that period, the ACN said. But it said French railway and subway fares have risen more sharply.
It estimated car-related revenue generated for the state totalled 316 billion francs last year, slightly more than the 310 billion raised from income tax.
